events.title: Constantine Wins the Battle of the Milvian Bridge
events.description: Outside Rome, Constantine I defeated his rival Maxentius. Maxentius drowned in the Tiber River during the retreat. The victory made Constantine the sole ruler of the Western Roman Empire.
events.significance: The victory is closely tied to Constantine's later support for Christianity, which changed the religious and political course of Europe.

events.title: Harvard University Is Founded
events.description: The colonial legislature of Massachusetts Bay voted to establish a college in what became Cambridge. It was the first institution of higher learning in the American colonies.
events.significance: Harvard grew into one of the world's best-known universities and set an early example for higher education in America.

events.title: The Statue of Liberty Is Dedicated
events.description: President Grover Cleveland presided over the dedication of the Statue of Liberty on Bedloe's Island in New York Harbor. The statue was a gift from France.
events.significance: The monument became a global symbol of freedom and a welcoming sight for millions of immigrants.

events.title: Czechoslovakia Declares Independence
events.description: As Austria-Hungary collapsed at the end of World War I, Czechoslovak leaders in Prague proclaimed an independent state. The declaration ended centuries of Habsburg rule over the Czech and Slovak lands.
events.significance: The new republic became one of Central Europe's few interwar democracies.

events.title: Khrushchev Orders Soviet Missiles Out of Cuba
events.description: Soviet Premier Nikita Khrushchev announced that Soviet missiles would be removed from Cuba. The announcement came after 13 tense days of confrontation with the United States.
events.significance: It ended the most dangerous moment of the Cold War, when the world came close to nuclear conflict.
